Saves computation by not modeling static areas with time-dependent fields [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that the method categorizes dynamic scene areas into static, deforming, and new, and models them with separate fields. Specifically, it notes that static areas are modeled by a stationary field $s(·)$ which does not depend on time $t$ (unlike the deformation and newness fields which take $(p, t)$ as input). Furthermore, the text explicitly mentions that this decomposition 'saves computation' by allowing the system to skip field forwarding for areas with low probability (using a threshold) and by using simpler representations (like a stationary field) for static areas, thereby reducing capacity and complexity.
